name: T-14 Armata

placement_rationale.text: T-14 Armata's own employment_notes are explicit that the type is effectively absent from confirmed combat use in Ukraine — reportedly kept out of theater rather than risked — so its 4 km placement should be read as a representative direct-fire MBT posture consistent with other tanks in this category (inside doctrine.md's lower-sky bracket of 1–1.5 km with local air/drone superiority to ~7 km without), not as a claim that a specific Armata has actually been positioned at that depth on the current front. This is the one asset in the batch where the placement number describes doctrine-typical siting for its class rather than an attested real deployment, worth flagging for anyone reading the map literally. (Nudged 4→3.6 km from this category's shared round-number value so it doesn't literally coincide with side_b-armor-t72 on the map's distance axis — a small, deterministic spread within the same band, not a new plausibility claim beyond what's already argued above.)

representative_system: T-14 Armata — Main battle tank (next-generation, limited fielding)

cost.display: Not publicly disclosed; unofficial estimates run well above $3-4M given low-rate production

key_facts.label: Crew
key_facts.value: Unmanned turret (crew in armored capsule in hull)

characteristics: Unmanned turret (crew in armored capsule in hull)
Strength: On paper, the most advanced Russian tank design; crew survivability concept (isolated capsule) is a genuine design advance

Limitation: Effectively absent from combat use in Ukraine as of available reporting; serial production reportedly minimal to non-existent; not risked in-theater, reportedly due to reputational cost of a combat loss
Estimated quantity available: ~20 units reported to exist; effectively none confirmed deployed to Ukraine
employment_notes: The clearest case in this catalog of a system that exists mainly in announcements rather than combat use — worth including specifically as a contrast to the T-90M/T-80BVM/T-72B3 entries, which are all combat-proven at scale
contrast_vs_traditional: Armata was designed to lead armored spearheads with an unmanned turret and active protection against guided munitions. Reporting on its combat record shows the opposite has happened — it has been kept mostly out of front-line engagement rather than leading assaults — which is itself evidence for the doctrine.md finding that exquisite, expensive platforms are the ones a drone-saturated front makes hardest to risk, not the ones best suited to dominate it.
